chunks: O Mu'awiya, when were you all protectors of the ruled and guardians of the affairs of the people?
Without any forward step or conspicuous distinction?
We seek Allah's protection against the befalling of previous misfortunes,
and I warn you lest you continue being deceived by desires and your appearance becomes different from your innerself.
ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's critique of Mu'awiya's rule in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) challenges Mu'awiya's claim to the caliphate by highlighting his lack of ancestral prestige or prior merit, contrasting him with the Prophet's family. He warns Mu'awiya against the illusion of stability, pointing out the dissonance between his public image and private reality, a critique central to the Shia view of the Umayyad usurpation. This letter serves as a foundational text for understanding the political and spiritual legitimacy crisis in early Islam.
